dedupe_keys.name: community driven ixps challenges and sustainable operating models in the asia pacific internet society 2025

description: This Internet Society report focuses on community-driven Internet exchange points, which support sustainable and resilient Internet infrastructure in developing regions. It explains that an IXP is a physical location where ISPs, enterprise networks and content delivery networks exchange traffic locally, cutting cost, latency and complexity, and compares commercial, nonprofit and community-driven models, arguing that each economy should have at least one community-driven IXP. The study examines the challenges these IXPs face, from limited access to financial resources to complex governance and operations, and the operational strategies and sustainable financial models used across the Asia-Pacific region. Producer: Internet Society, 2025. Coverage: Asia-Pacific, with a global preview. Access: the landing page was read; the full paper is a separate download that was not opened. Licence and cost: free; licence not stated. Caveats: the findings and any IXP-level numbers were not read, so the record is based on the summary. Simulation uses: the operating models and cost challenges inform capacity-planning and governance scenarios for exchange points. Related records: the Internet Society Pulse platform (data-internet-society-pulse) and the PCH IXP policy documents guide (data-pch-ixp-policy-documents-guide).
